senses.def: A diminutive of the male given name Xavier.
A member of the Xaverian Brothers, a religious order founded in Bruges, Belgium 1839 and dedicated to Catholic education.
Pertaining or related to this religious order.
A diminutive of the male given name Xavier.
Spanish missionary and Jesuit who establish missionaries in Japan and Ceylon and the East Indies (1506-1552)
A male given name from Spanish [in turn from Basque].
A surname from Spanish [in turn from Basque], found chiefly among people of Spanish and Portuguese descent.
Any of various notable people with this name as given name or surname, especially Saint Francis Xavier, a Spanish Catholic saint and missionary (1506–1552).
An Italian chicken soup with parmesan dumplings.
Resembling or characteristic of Professor Charles Xavier, a Marvel telepath, most notable for being the primary leader of the X-Men.
The ideology of Professor Charles Xavier, advocating peaceful coexistence between humans and mutants, typically emphasizing nonviolence, integration, and moral restraint.
A student who attends any of numerous schools named for Saint Francis Xavier.
One of the Xavánte, a native people of central Brazil.
A Ge language spoken by the Xavánte people in and surrounding eastern Mato Grosso, Brazil.
